5d:["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"ORB-SLAM3"}]," (Campos et al., 2021) is feature-based and map-centric: ORB descriptors, three\nparallel threads, and an ",["$","em",null,{"children":"Atlas"}]," of sub-maps so that losing tracking starts a new map instead of\ncorrupting the old one. Its visual-inertial contribution is to make the IMU initialization itself a\nmaximum-a-posteriori problem rather than a heuristic, and its reported accuracy on the standard\ndrone benchmarks — an average of 3.6 cm on EuRoC for the stereo-inertial configuration — is what\nmade \"2 to 5 times more accurate than previous approaches\" a defensible claim rather than marketing."]}]
5e:["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"VINS-Mono / VINS-Fusion"}]," (Qin, Li & Shen, 2018) is optical-flow-based and window-centric: KLT\ntracks, a loosely-coupled bootstrap that aligns a vision-only reconstruction with the preintegrated\nIMU to recover scale and gravity, then a tightly-coupled sliding window whose past is a\nmarginalization prior, and finally a global pose graph that optimizes only four degrees of freedom\nbecause gravity has already fixed roll and pitch."]}]
5f:["$","p",null,{"children":"Read the two columns of that figure again. There is not one block in either system that this book\nhas not built: a measurement model, a manifold retraction, a sparse least-squares solve, an\nelimination, a loop closure. The systems are hard because integration is hard — thread safety,\ninitialization corner cases, feature-track bookkeeping — not because the estimation theory is\ndeeper than what you have just derived."}]
